notes: TEST profile (no patterns): software developer in her 30s working from home, works in the study room on weekdays, lunch in the kitchen, gym some evenings. Written by hand to test the engine; no data.

windowSensors.reason: One sensor on the living-room window from a starter kit.

behaviours.description: Wake up on weekdays and unplug the phone.
Wake up on weekdays and unplug the phone.
Bathroom, breakfast in the kitchen, open the living-room curtain, back to the bedroom.
Work in the study room in the morning.
Lunch in the kitchen and dining room.
Work in the study room in the afternoon.
On arriving home: entryway light on if the entryway is dark, off again before going in; living-room light on if the living room is dark.
Music off and earbuds out on arrival.
Close the living-room curtain when it gets dark outside.
TV in the living room in the evening.

Ordinary phone use while awake. About 39 uses a day from this rule (Winbush et al. 2025, 10,099 US adults: median 1.71 unlocks per hour, 41 a day) and about 5 hours of app time a day (data.ai Korea Q1 2022: 5.2 h). A university student: more video and social media than the Korean all-age per-app averages (WiseApp 2025).
Straight to bed after a late arrival.
Go to bed: bedroom, phone on the charger, sleep.

sources.unlocksPerHour, appMinutesPerHour: Winbush et al. 2025, PNAS 122(43) e2427311122, 10,099 US adults, Android

sources.manualScreenOff: assumption: beta(4.5, 0.5); Hintze et al. 2014: some always switch off by hand, some almost never
sources.glancesPerDay: Hintze et al. 2014 (UbiComp): locked sessions median 22, mean 33 a day
sources.dailySigma: Appiah et al. 2026 (J Technol Behav Sci): within-person CV of daily unlocks mostly > 25%, examples 16% and 60%; StudentLife 2013
